r.정치 구도: A presidential system modeled on that of the United States, in which the president serves a single six-year term. The president and vice president are elected separately, so they can come from rival camps. Local political dynasties matter more than parties, and members of the same family often hold the posts of mayor, legislator and even president across generations. In 2022 two powerful political families joined forces to win the presidency and vice presidency, but they soon split, and the feud between the two camps now dominates politics. In March 2025 the former president who led the 'war on drugs' was arrested on a warrant from the International Criminal Court and flown to The Hague, and in April 2026 the court committed him to trial on charges of crimes against humanity. Since 2025 a huge corruption scandal over flood-control budgets has sparked mass protests, and impeachment complaints have been filed against both the president and the vice president.

t.why: Sitting on the eastern edge of the South China Sea, it clashes more often than any other country with China, which claims most of that sea as its own. In 2016 an international arbitral tribunal ruled that China's claims had no legal basis, but Beijing rejects the ruling, and Chinese vessels keep firing water cannon at Philippine boats. It has been a US treaty ally since a 1951 mutual defense treaty, and in 2023 it expanded the number of Philippine bases US forces can use to nine. Its northernmost islands lie very close to Taiwan, so any crisis in the Taiwan Strait would affect it directly. As ASEAN chair in 2026, it is pushing to conclude negotiations on a code of conduct for the South China Sea. With so many of its citizens working abroad, protecting them becomes a major task whenever conflict breaks out in places like the Middle East.
t.rel: A US ally that often clashes with the Chinese coast guard over islands and reefs in the South China Sea. It won an international arbitration case in 2016, but China rejects the ruling.
t.korea: Diplomatic relations were established in March 1949, making the Philippines the fifth country to recognize the Republic of Korea. In the Korean War it was the first Asian country to answer the call for troops, sending more than 7,400 soldiers. The two countries upgraded ties to a strategic partnership in 2024, and their free trade agreement took effect on December 31 that year. HD Hyundai has leased the Subic shipyard, once run by Hanjin Heavy Industries until it went bankrupt in 2019, and is building ships there again. It is a popular destination for Korean travelers, and many Korean students go there to learn English.
t.know: Banana ketchup, a Filipino favorite, was invented during World War II when tomatoes ran short.
etext: Millions of Filipinos work abroad as seafarers, nurses and domestic workers across the Middle East, the United States and Asia, and the money they send home underpins household spending.

Good English and low labor costs mean it handles a great deal of business process outsourcing for US companies, from call centers to accounting and medical records. Together with India it is one of the world's two great hubs for this work. The risk is that AI could take over simple customer-service jobs.

It mines more nickel ore than any country except Indonesia, selling most of it to China. A young population of more than 100 million supports large consumer industries such as shopping malls, telecoms and banking.

Manufacturing is weaker than in its neighbors, so good jobs are scarce. Electricity is among the most expensive in Southeast Asia, typhoons and floods cause heavy damage every year, and its many islands make transport costly.
